```{r}
  select(-c(percent_overlap, directory)) %>%
  left_join(meta.lipid %>%
              select(filename, split, num_vertices),
            by = join_by(filename)) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(num_vertices))

rm(meta.lipid, meta.prosome)

calc_r2 <- function(x, y) {
  if (is.numeric(x) && is.numeric(y) && length(na.omit(x)) > 1 && length(na.omit(y)) > 1) {
    df <- data.frame(x = x, y = y)
    model <- lm(y ~ x, data = df, na.action = na.omit)
    return(round(summary(model)$r.squared, 3))
  } else {
    return(NA) # Return NA if column is not numeric or has insufficient data
  }
}
```

# Train vs Test data

## Prosome results
- compare pixels, axes
- plot size/pixels vs accuracy
- separate test and train
```{r}
# Summary stats
res.prosome %>% 
  filter(prosome_pixels_predicted != 0) %>% 
  group_by(split) %>% 
  summarise(n = n(),
            IoU.mean = mean(IoU),
            IoU.median = median(IoU),
            Recall.mean = mean(Recall),
            F1score.mean = mean(F1score),
            .groups = "drop")


# Is accuracy related to how "complex" the polygon mask is?
ggplot(res.prosome, aes(x = num_vertices,
                        y = IoU,
                        color = split)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") 

cowplot::plot_grid(

                          color = split)) +
```

## Lipids results
### Compare cropped prosome vs original image
```{r, eval=FALSE}
res.lipid %>% 
  group_by(split) %>% 
  summarise(n = n(),
            IoU.mean = mean(IoU),
            IoU.median = median(IoU),
            Recall.mean = mean(Recall),
            F1score.mean = mean(F1score, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")
res.lipid.crop %>% 
  group_by(split) %>% 
  summarise(n = n(),
            IoU.mean = mean(IoU),
            IoU.median = median(IoU),
            Recall.mean = mean(Recall),
            F1score.mean = mean(F1score, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

# Compare metrics for with cropped prosome or not
comp.lipids <- res.lipid %>% 
  mutate(model = "original image") %>% 
  # pivot_longer(cols = lipid_pixels_annotated:F1score,
  #              names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>% 
  left_join(res.lipid.crop %>% 
              mutate(model = "cropped prosome"),
            by = join_by(filename, split, num_vertices))

# Model performance is OFTEN (but not always) better when prosome is cropped. The cropped-prosome model can perform really well even when the original image model has poor performance
cowplot::plot_grid(
  ggplot(comp.lipids, aes(x = lipid_pixels_predicted.x, 
                          y = lipid_pixels_predicted.y, color = split)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    xlab("lipid predicted no crop") + 
    ylab("lipid predicted with crop") +
    geom_abline(),
  
  ggplot(comp.lipids, aes(x = IoU.x, y = IoU.y, color = split)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
    xlab("IoU no crop") + 
    ylab("IoU with crop") +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    geom_abline(),
  
  ggplot(comp.lipids, aes(x = Recall.x, y = Recall.y, color = split)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
    xlab("Recall no crop") + 
    ylab("Recall with crop") +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    geom_abline(),
  
  ggplot(comp.lipids, aes(x = F1score.x, y = F1score.y, color = split)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
    xlab("F1 score no crop") + 
    ylab("F1 score with crop") +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    geom_abline(),
  rel_heights = c(1,1.2)
)



ggsave("figures/UVP6_prosome_crop_comparison.png",
       heigh = 5, width = 7, units = "in")
```

## Lipid fullness: Combine prosome and lipid, calculate fullness and plot distributions
```{r}
res.lf.all <- res.lipid.crop %>% 
  select(filename, lipid_pixels_annotated:lipid_mass_predicted, IoU) %>% 
  left_join(select(res.prosome,
                   filename, prosome_pixels_annotated,
                   prosome_pixels_predicted),
            by = join_by(filename)) %>% 
  mutate(lipidfullness_annotated = lipid_pixels_annotated/prosome_pixels_annotated*100,
         lipidfullness_predicted = lipid_pixels_predicted/prosome_pixels_predicted*100) %>% 
  mutate(object_id = str_remove(filename,".png"))

# The range of values of the annotated data
res.anot.range <- res.lf.all %>%
  select(lipid = lipid_pixels_annotated, prosome = prosome_pixels_annotated,
         lipidfullness = lipidfullness_annotated) %>% 
  summarise(across(everything(), list(
    min = ~min(., na.rm = TRUE),
    max = ~max(., na.rm = TRUE),
    mean = ~mean(., na.rm = TRUE),
    median = ~median(., na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = ~sd(., na.rm = TRUE),
    n = ~sum(!is.na(.)) # Count of non-NA values
  ), .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"))
  # pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "statistic", values_to = "value") %>%
  # separate(statistic, into = c("column", "metric"), sep = "_") %>% 
  # pivot_wider(names_from = metric, values_from = value)


# Remove instances when the lipid predicted is obviously wrong and small
res.lf <- res.lf.all %>% 
  filter(lipid_pixels_predicted >= res.anot.range$lipid_min &
           lipid_pixels_predicted <= res.anot.range$lipid_max) %>% 
  filter(prosome_pixels_predicted >= res.anot.range$prosome_min &
           prosome_pixels_predicted <= res.anot.range$prosome_max)  %>% 
  filter(lipidfullness_predicted >= res.anot.range$lipidfullness_min &
           lipidfullness_predicted <= res.anot.range$lipidfullness_max) %>%
  # Calculate residual error in lipidfullness for comparison with lipid IoU
  mutate(fullness_residual = abs(lipidfullness_predicted-lipidfullness_annotated))

cowplot::plot_grid(
  ggplot(res.lf, aes(x = lipid_pixels_annotated, y = lipidfullness_annotated)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
    annotate("text", x = max(res.lf$lipid_pixels_annotated, na.rm = TRUE),
             y = min(res.lf$lipidfullness_annotated, na.rm = TRUE),
             label = paste0("R² = ", calc_r2(res.lf$lipid_pixels_annotated,
                                             res.lf$lipidfullness_annotated)),
             hjust = 1, vjust = 0, size = 5),
  
  
  ggplot(res.lf, aes(x = lipid_pixels_predicted, y = lipidfullness_predicted)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm")  +
    annotate("text", x = max(res.lf$lipid_pixels_predicted, na.rm = TRUE),
             y = min(res.lf$lipidfullness_predicted, na.rm = TRUE),
             label = paste0("R² = ", calc_r2(res.lf$lipid_pixels_predicted,
                                             res.lf$lipidfullness_predicted)),
             hjust = 1, vjust = 0, size = 5),
  
  
  # ggplot(res.lf, aes(x = lipidfullness_annotated, y = IoU)) +
  #   geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  #   geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  #   annotate("text", x = max(res.lf$lipidfullness_annotated, na.rm = TRUE),
  #            y = min(res.lf$IoU, na.rm = TRUE),
  #            label = paste0("R² = ", calc_r2(res.lf$lipidfullness_annotated,
  #                                            res.lf$IoU)),
  #            hjust = 1, vjust = 0, size = 5),
  
  # TODO Why is the predicted lipid fullness a bad fit when the predicted pixels are good? Because predicted prosome is slightly larger and predicted lipids slightly smaller??
  ggplot(res.lf, aes(x = lipidfullness_annotated, y = lipidfullness_predicted)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
    geom_abline() +
    annotate("text", x = max(res.lf$lipidfullness_annotated, na.rm = TRUE),
             y = min(res.lf$lipidfullness_predicted, na.rm = TRUE),
             label = paste0("R² = ", calc_r2(res.lf$lipidfullness_annotated,
                                             res.lf$lipidfullness_predicted)),
             hjust = 1, vjust = 0, size = 5),
  
   ggplot(res.lf , aes(x = fullness_residual, y = IoU)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
    annotate("text", x = max(res.lf$fullness_residual, na.rm = TRUE),
             y = min(res.lf$IoU, na.rm = TRUE),
             label = paste0("R² = ", calc_r2(res.lf$fullness_residual,
                                             res.lf$IoU)),
             hjust = 1, vjust = 0, size = 5) +
   ylab("Lipid IoU"),

  
  nrow = 2, labels = "auto"
)


ggsave("figures/UVP6_lipidfullness_evaluation2.png",
       heigh = 5, width = 7, units = "in")
```


## TODO Residual distribution
- Negative prosome-LF residual relationship mean that the predicted LF are larger when the predicted prosomes are smaller, while positive lipid-LF residual relationship mean that larger predicted lipid result in high LF.
```{r}
residual.check <- res.lf %>% 
  mutate(prosome_residual = prosome_pixels_predicted - prosome_pixels_annotated,
         lipid_residual = lipid_pixels_predicted - lipid_pixels_annotated,
         fullness_residual = lipidfullness_predicted-lipidfullness_annotated)

ggplot(residual.check, aes(x = prosome_residual, y = fullness_residual)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +

ggplot(residual.check, aes(x = lipid_residual, y = fullness_residual)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")

ggplot(residual.check, aes(x = fullness_residual)) +
```

### Open images at extremes
```{r, eval=FALSE}

# uvp6_meta.new.extrap <- uvp6_meta.new  %>% 
#   # filter(lipidpcrop_pixels_predicted > 2000) %>% 
#   filter(Major < min_major | Major > max_major) %>%
#   # complete the filenames
#   mutate(filename = paste0(cnn_outfol, object_id, "_overlapRGB.png"))

# Function to display the images
open_images <- function(filenames) {
  for (file in filenames) {
    if (file.exists(file)) {
      if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") {
        shell.exec(file)  # Opens the image in the default viewer on Windows
      } else {
        system(paste("xdg-open", shQuote(file)), wait = FALSE)  # Linux
        system(paste("open", shQuote(file)), wait = FALSE)  # macOS
      }
    } else {
      message(paste("File not found:", file))
    }
  }
}


# Prosomes
```

# Morphotraits as predictors for segmentation quality
## Load morphotrait data
```{r}
# Morphotraits and other sample information
uvp6_de_side <- read.table("../../Laval-imaging-analysis/UVP6_darkedge/ecotaxa_export_5108_20241018_1521.tsv", sep = '\t', header = TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(dataset = "darkedge2021_vislipid_side")
uvp6_de_top <- read.table("../../Laval-imaging-analysis/UVP6_darkedge/ecotaxa_export_5108_20241018_1518.tsv", sep = '\t', header = TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(dataset = "darkedge2021_vislipid_top")
uvp6_de_calanus <- read.table("../../Laval-imaging-analysis/UVP6_darkedge/export_5108_20250311_1406_Calanus_no_visible_lipid_sac/ecotaxa_export_5108_20250311_1406.tsv", sep = '\t', header = TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(dataset = "darkedge2021_calanus")


# Only "Calanus" so far for UVP6 Amund 2023
uvp6_amund <- read.table("../../Laval-imaging-analysis/UVP6_amundsen2023/Calanus/ecotaxa_export_10101_20250117_1943.tsv",sep = '\t', header = TRUE) %>% 
  mutate(dataset = "amundsen2023_calanus")


uvp6_meta <- bind_rows(uvp6_de_side, uvp6_de_top, uvp6_de_calanus, uvp6_amund) %>% 
  filter(img_rank == 100)
rm(uvp6_de_side, uvp6_de_top, uvp6_de_calanus, uvp6_amund)

# rename object_id for matching with the ecotaxa metadata
res.prosome <- res.prosome %>%
  mutate(object_id = str_remove(filename,".png"))
res.lipid.crop <- res.lipid.crop %>%
  mutate(object_id = str_remove(filename,".png"))
res.lf <- res.lf %>% 
  mutate(object_id = str_remove(filename,".png"))

# subset to files found in res.lipid.crop OR res.prosome
uvp6_meta.sub <- uvp6_meta %>% 
  filter(object_id %in% res.lf$object_id) %>% 
  # filter(object_id %in% res.lipid.crop$object_id | 
  #          object_id %in% res.prosome$object_id) %>% 
  select(object_id,
         lat = object_lat, lon = object_lon, depth = object_depth_min,
         date = object_date, time = object_time,
         annotation = object_annotation_category, sample_id, sample_cruise,
         Major = object_major, Minor = object_minor, Perim. = object_perim.,
         Feret = object_feret, Area = object_area, Elongation = object_elongation,
         Ver.Sym. = object_symetriev, Ver.Sym.2 = object_symetrievc, 
         Circ. = object_circ., Thickr = object_thickr, 
         Mean.grey = object_mean, Med.grey = object_median,
         `Hist.grey 75%` = object_histcum3, 
         Sdev.grey = object_stddev, Skew.grey = object_skew,
         Fractal = object_fractal, 
         `Perim./Feret` = object_perimferet,
         `Perim./Major` = object_perimmajor)
```

## Major, Minor, Biovolume
- the segmentations are unrealistic if the predicted major axis is outside the confidence range of the morphotrait major axis
- also if the image is circular, it is probably not the best imaging angle captured
```{r}
# Compile major axis information
df <- uvp6_meta.sub %>% 
  select(object_id, Major, Minor, Feret) %>% 
  left_join(select(res.prosome, object_id, IoU.prosome = IoU,
                   prosome_major_annotated, prosome_major_predicted,
                   prosome_minor_annotated, prosome_minor_predicted),
            by = "object_id") %>% 
  left_join(select(res.lipid.crop, object_id, IoU.lipid = IoU,
                   lipid_major_annotated, lipid_major_predicted),
            by = "object_id") %>% 
  # add the fullness info if needed
  left_join(res.lf %>% select(-IoU),
            by = "object_id") %>% 
  # add "derived" major axis as pixel_area/major=
    mutate(prosome_minor_derived_anot = (prosome_pixels_annotated / 
            (pi * prosome_major_annotated/2)) * 2) %>% 
    mutate(prosome_minor_derived_pred = (prosome_pixels_predicted / 
            (pi * prosome_major_predicted/2)) * 2) %>% 
  # TODO calculate biovolumes based on spheroid (4/3 * pi * a * b * c)
  mutate(biovolume_EcoTaxa = (4/3) * pi * (Major/2) * (Minor/2)^2,
         biovolume_annotated = (4/3) * pi * (prosome_major_annotated/2) * (prosome_minor_annotated/2)^2,
         biovolume_predicted = (4/3) * pi * (prosome_major_predicted/2) * (prosome_minor_predicted/2)^2,
         biovolume_annotated_deriv = (4/3) * pi * (prosome_major_annotated/2) * (prosome_minor_derived_anot/2)^2,
         biovolume_predicted_deriv = (4/3) * pi * (prosome_major_predicted/2) * (prosome_minor_derived_pred/2)^2)


df2 <- df %>% 
  select(object_id, annotated = prosome_major_annotated, 
         predicted = prosome_major_predicted,
         EcoTaxa = Major) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(predicted, EcoTaxa),
               names_to = "method", values_to = "value") %>% 
  # convert pixles to mm3
  mutate(value = value * 0.023,
         annotated = annotated * 0.023) %>% 
  mutate(method = factor(method, levels = c("predicted","EcoTaxa")))

p2 <- ggplot(df2, aes(x = annotated,
                      y = value, color = method)) +
  geom_abline() +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  xlab("Major axis annotated (mm)") + ylab("Major axis (mm)") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom") 

df3 <- df %>% 
  select(object_id, annotated = prosome_minor_annotated, 
         predicted = prosome_minor_predicted,
         EcoTaxa = Minor, 
         annotated_deriv = prosome_minor_derived_anot,
         predicted_deriv = prosome_minor_derived_pred) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(predicted, EcoTaxa, 
                        annotated_deriv, predicted_deriv),
               names_to = "method", values_to = "value") %>% 
  # convert pixles to mm3
  mutate(value = value * 0.023,
         annotated = annotated * 0.023) %>% 
  mutate(method = factor(method, levels = c("predicted","EcoTaxa",
                                          "annotated_deriv","predicted_deriv")))

p3 <- ggplot(df3, aes(x = annotated,
                      y = value, color = method)) +
  geom_abline() +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  xlab("Minor axis annotated (mm)") + ylab("Minor axis (mm)") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")


# Plot all biovolumes against best guess (major, derived_minor of annotated)
df4 <- df %>% 
  select(object_id, biovolume_EcoTaxa:biovolume_predicted_deriv) %>% 
  relocate(object_id, biovolume_annotated) %>% 
  pivot_longer(biovolume_EcoTaxa:biovolume_predicted_deriv,
               names_to = "method", values_to = "value") %>% 
  mutate(method = str_remove(method, "biovolume_")) %>% 
  # convert pixles to mm3
  mutate(value = value * (0.023^3),
         biovolume_annotated = biovolume_annotated * (0.023^3)) %>% 
  mutate(method = factor(method, levels = c("predicted","EcoTaxa",
                                          "annotated_deriv","predicted_deriv")))

p4 <- ggplot(df4, aes(x = biovolume_annotated,
                      y = value, color = method)) +
  geom_abline() +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  xlab("Biovolume based on annotated axes (mm^3)") + ylab("Biovolume (mm^3)") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

cowplot::plot_grid(p2, p3, p4, ncol = 1, labels = "auto")


ggsave("figures/UVP6_major_minor_biovolume2.png",
       heigh = 9, width = 6, units = "in")

p3
```

## Find which column can be used as a linear/loess predictor of the accuracy
- No good R2 with a linear model.
- Still no good one with loess with highest R2 between Area and IoU.prosome
```{r}
# Function to calculate R² using nonparametric LOESS fit
calc_r2_loess <- function(x, y) {
  if (is.numeric(x) && is.numeric(y) && length(na.omit(x)) > 1 && length(na.omit(y)) > 1) {
    loess_fit <- loess(y ~ x, na.action = na.omit)
    y_pred <- predict(loess_fit, x)
    r2 <- 1 - sum((y - y_pred)^2, na.rm = TRUE) / sum((y - mean(y, na.rm = TRUE))^2, na.rm = TRUE)
    return(round(r2, 3))
  } else {
    return(NA)
  }
}

df <- uvp6_meta.sub %>%
  select(object_id, Major:`Perim./Major`) %>% 
  left_join(select(res.prosome, object_id, IoU.prosome = IoU),
            by = "object_id") %>% 
  left_join(select(res.lipid.crop, object_id, IoU.lipid = IoU),
            by = "object_id")


# Compute R² values relative to IoU.prosome
r2_prosome <- df %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), ~ calc_r2_loess(.x, df$IoU.prosome), .names = "{.col}")) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "Column", values_to = "R2_vs_IoU.prosome")

# Compute R² values relative to IoU.lipid
r2_lipid <- df %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), ~ calc_r2_loess(.x, df$IoU.lipid), .names = "{.col}")) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "Column", values_to = "R2_vs_IoU.lipid")

# Combine both R² results into a single table
r2_table <- full_join(r2_prosome, r2_lipid, by = "Column") %>% 
  filter(Column %notin% c("IoU.lipid", "IoU.prosome"))


```


## Get the minimum values of morphotraits for images segmented
```{r}
# TODO Change the source of prosome_annotated to the full range

uvp6_sub_table <- uvp6_meta.sub %>%
  select(object_id,Major:`Perim./Major`) %>% 
  left_join(res.lf %>% 
              select(object_id, lipid = lipid_pixels_annotated, 
                     prosome = prosome_pixels_annotated, 
                     lipidfullness = lipidfullness_annotated),
            by = "object_id") %>% 
  select(-object_id) %>% 
  summarise(across(everything(), list(
    min = ~min(., na.rm = TRUE),
    max = ~max(., na.rm = TRUE),
    mean = ~mean(., na.rm = TRUE),
    median = ~median(., na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = ~sd(., na.rm = TRUE),
    n = ~sum(!is.na(.)) # Count of non-NA values
  ), .names = "{.col}_{.fn}")) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "statistic", values_to = "value") %>%
  separate(statistic, into = c("column", "metric"), sep = "_") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = metric, values_from = value)
```

## Curate and organize
```{r}
df.temp <- res.lipid.crop %>% 
  select(object_id, lipid_pixels_annotated, lipid_pixels_predicted) %>% 
  full_join(res.prosome %>% 
              select(object_id, 
                     prosome_pixels_annotated, prosome_pixels_predicted),
            by = "object_id") %>% 
  # Predicted prosome area < 200 pixels are smaller than what is observed
  mutate(prosome_pixels_predicted = if_else(prosome_pixels_predicted < 200,
         NA, prosome_pixels_predicted)) %>% 
  # Calculate lipid fullness
    mutate(lipidfullness_annotated = lipid_pixels_annotated/prosome_pixels_annotated*100,
         lipidfullness_predicted = lipid_pixels_predicted/prosome_pixels_predicted*100)  

# Lengthen to [object, prosome, lipid, lipidfullness, annotated/predicted]
# Note that there are instances here when there is annotated prosome but no annotated lipid, for simplicity, exclude them here and use the predicted prosome for these images instead so that there will be matching predicted lipids.
uvp6_annot <- bind_rows(
  df.temp %>% 
    select(object_id, prosome = prosome_pixels_annotated,
           lipid = lipid_pixels_annotated, 
           lipidfullness = lipidfullness_annotated) %>% 
    mutate(type = "annotated"),
  
  df.temp %>% 
    select(object_id, prosome = prosome_pixels_predicted,
           lipid = lipid_pixels_predicted, 
           lipidfullness = lipidfullness_predicted) %>% 
    mutate(type = "predicted") %>% 
    filter(object_id %in% res.lf$object_id),
) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(lipidfullness))

uvp6_pred <- newimgs %>% 
  filter(object_id %notin% to_exclude$object_id) %>% 
  select(object_id, prosome = prosome_pixels_predicted,
         lipid = lipidpcrop_pixels_predicted,
         lipidfullness = lipidfullness2,
         type = predLipidSac)

# Combine and add metadata (n = 8394)
uvp6_all <- bind_rows(uvp6_annot, uvp6_pred) %>% 
  left_join(uvp6_meta %>% 
              select(object_id,
                     lat = object_lat, lon = object_lon, 
                     depth = object_depth_min,
                     date = object_date, time = object_time,
                     annotation = object_annotation_category, 
                     sample_id, sample_cruise,
                     Major = object_major, Minor = object_minor, 
                     Perim = object_perim.,
                     Feret = object_feret, Area = object_area, 
                     Elongation = object_elongation,
                     VerSym = object_symetriev, VerSym2 = object_symetrievc, 
                     Circ = object_circ., Thickr = object_thickr, 
                     MeanGrey = object_mean, MedGrey = object_median,
                     HistGrey75 = object_histcum3, SdevGrey = object_stddev, 
                     SkewGrey = object_skew,Fractal = object_fractal, 
                     PerimFeret = object_perimferet, 
                     PerimMajor = object_perimmajor),
            by = "object_id") %>% 
  # Add the volumes matching the 5m depth bins
  mutate(Depth_5m = floor(depth / 5)*5+2.5) %>% 
  left_join(uvp6_volumes,
            by = join_by(sample_id, Depth_5m)) %>% 
  # rename and level the method type facors
  mutate(type = if_else(type == "cant segment",
                        "not visible", type),
         type = if_else(type == "lipid sac",
                        "visible",type)) %>% 
  mutate(type = factor(type, levels = c("annotated","predicted",
                                        "visible","not visible")))
  
rm(uvp6_annot, uvp6_pred, df.temp)

cowplot::plot_grid(

The new data that were classified as with lipid sac, generally follows that distribution, although the mode is slightly higher. However, the images identified as "cant segment lipid sac" had more images predicted to have smaller lipid sacs and a significantly different distribution. T
  ggplot(uvp6_all, aes(x = lipid, fill = type, color = type)) +
```

## Inspect likely erroneous segmentations
- copepods smaller and larger than what was in the training data, which technically are extrapolations (now, no larger instances)... resolve to remove all images that are smaller than what was trained
```{r, eval=FALSE}
min_major <- filter(uvp6_sub_table, column == "Major")$min
max_major <- filter(uvp6_sub_table, column == "Major")$max

cnn_outfol <- "C:/Users/patri/python_workspace/copepods-lipid-content/prediction_outputs/model_resnet34_prosomeUVP6_deamundp2/"

uvp6_meta.new.extrap <- uvp6_meta.new  %>% 
  # filter(lipidpcrop_pixels_predicted > 2000) %>% 
  filter(Major < min_major | Major > max_major) %>%
  # complete the filenames
  mutate(filename = paste0(cnn_outfol, object_id, "_overlapRGB.png"))

# Display the images
open_images <- function(filenames) {
  for (file in filenames) {
    if (file.exists(file)) {
      if (.Platform$OS.type == "windows") {
        shell.exec(file)  # Opens the image in the default viewer on Windows
      } else {
        system(paste("xdg-open", shQuote(file)), wait = FALSE)  # Linux
        system(paste("open", shQuote(file)), wait = FALSE)  # macOS
      }
    } else {
      message(paste("File not found:", file))
    }
  }
}
open_images(uvp6_meta.new.extrap$filename[1:4])
```


# Does the UVP6 model work with the downscaled LOKI by 1/4?
The model trained on the UVP6 data tends to overestimate the lipid content of the downscaled LOKI images. Maybe this is because the downscaled LOKI resolution is actually coarser at 92 um versus the 84 um uvp 6 resolution, which means images are smaller for the downscaled UVP.
```{r, eval=FALSE}
res.loki4 <- read.csv("C:/Users/patri/python_workspace/copepods-lipid-content/prediction_outputs/model_resnet34_lokid4/new_predictions_LOKId4_20250319.csv")

# how many images did the classification model predicted that a lipid sac can't be identified? Ideally this should be close to zero since all these images were manually segmented for lipid sacs but for the full resolution LOKI images
res.loki4 %>% 
  group_by(predLipidSac) %>% 
  summarise(count = n(),
            conf_no = mean(prob_0),
            conf_yes = mean(prob_1),
            .groups = "drop")

sum.loki4 <- res.loki4 %>% 
  group_by(predLipidSac) %>% 
  summarise(n = n(),
            IoU.mean = mean(IoU),
            Recall.mean = mean(Recall),
            F1score.mean = mean(F1score, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")

ggplot(res.loki4, aes(x = lipid_pixels_annotated, 
                      y = lipidpcrop_pixels_predicted,
                      color = predLipidSac)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_abline()

cowplot::plot_grid(
  ggplot(res.loki4, aes(x = lipid_pixels_annotated, 
                        y = IoU,
                        color = predLipidSac)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
    geom_smooth() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 80, linetype = "dashed", color = "orange") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 90, linetype = "longdash", color = "orange"),
  
  
  ggplot(res.loki4, aes(x = lipidpcrop_pixels_predicted, 
                        y = IoU,
                        color = predLipidSac)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
    geom_smooth() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 80, linetype = "dashed", color = "orange") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 90, linetype = "longdash", color = "orange")
)
```
